**Divide the sequence, but still let each query see every permitted key.** Each worker keeps a block of query positions. Key/value blocks circulate among workers. When a block arrives, the worker computes that block's contribution to its local query outputs and combines it with contributions already processed. [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.01889) [2](https://jax-ml.github.io/scaling-book/)

The subtlety is softmax normalization. Softmax over each block separately and then averaging the outputs would be wrong because blocks do not generally have equal total probability mass. Instead maintain a running maximum, a rescaled exponential sum, and a rescaled value-weighted numerator.

**A tiny example.** If one query has scores 0 in the first block and log(3) in the second, the global probabilities are 1/4 and 3/4. Treating each single-element block as a complete softmax would give probability one within both blocks, losing their relative weights. Online softmax retains that cross-block normalization and returns the same dense attention result up to numerical rounding.

Sharding reduces per-device activation storage and avoids materializing the entire score matrix on one GPU. It does not remove dense attention's quadratic number of query-key interactions. Global position-aware masking, backward communication, and enough computation to overlap transfers are essential. A million-token sequence fitting across devices is a memory achievement; whether training it is affordable remains a separate compute and network question.

**Technical details and references.**

Context parallelism assigns different query-token blocks to different devices. Key/value blocks circulate through a ring; each rank updates its local attention outputs using online softmax statistics across blocks. It never needs the complete score matrix at once. [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.01889) [2](https://jax-ml.github.io/scaling-book/)

$$m'=\max(m,m_b),\quad \ell'=e^{m-m'}\ell+e^{m_b-m'}\ell_b.$$

The weighted numerator is rescaled analogously, preserving dense attention semantics up to rounding. Causal masks and backward communication must reflect global token positions. This distributes activation storage, but full attention still has quadratic arithmetic; a million-token sequence is not made cheap by sharding alone. Communication must overlap enough block compute to help. Compare ring bandwidth, per-rank memory, imbalance, and recomputation with sparse or recurrent alternatives when exact dense attention is unnecessary.
